legend: You are the master of an arena with n$$$n$$$ fighters under your control, numbered from 1$$$1$$$ to n$$$n$$$. Fighter 1$$$1$$$ is your favourite—you want them to emerge as the sole champion.
You are given an n×n$$$n\times n$$$ matrix M$$$M$$$. For i≠j$$$i\neq j$$$:
Mi,j=1$$$M_{i,j}=\texttt{1}$$$ means fighter i$$$i$$$ definitely beats fighter j$$$j$$$.
Mi,j=0$$$M_{i,j}=\texttt{0}$$$ means fighter i$$$i$$$ definitely loses to fighter j$$$j$$$.
Mi,j=?$$$M_{i,j}=\texttt{?}$$$ means the outcome is undecided and you may choose it.

It is guaranteed that Mi,i=0$$$M_{i,i} = \texttt{0}$$$ for all i$$$i$$$, and for all i≠j$$$i \ne j$$$, the pair (Mi,j,Mj,i)$$$(M_{i,j}, M_{j,i})$$$ is one of: (1,0)$$$(\texttt{1}, \texttt{0})$$$, (0,1)$$$(\texttt{0}, \texttt{1})$$$, or (?,?)$$$(\texttt{?}, \texttt{?})$$$.

You must schedule exactly n−1$$$n-1$$$ one-on-one matches so that in the end exactly one fighter remains undefeated, and that fighter must be number 1$$$1$$$. A fighter may appear in multiple matches (until eliminated).

Decide any choices for the '?' entries and output a sequence of n−1$$$n-1$$$ matches (a,b)$$$(a,b)$$$ meaning "a$$$a$$$ defeats b$$$b$$$". If it's impossible to make fighter 1 the unique champion, print No$$$\textbf{No}$$$.
input: The first line contains a single integer t$$$t$$$ (1≤t≤500)$$$(1 \le t \le 500)$$$ — the number of test cases.
The first line of each test case contains integer n$$$n$$$ (2≤n≤1000$$$2\le n\le 1000$$$) — the number of fighters.
Then in each test case follow n$$$n$$$ lines each with a string of length n$$$n$$$, the i$$$i$$$-th line being Mi,1Mi,2…Mi,n$$$M_{i,1}M_{i,2}\dots M_{i,n}$$$.
It is guaranteed that the sum of n$$$n$$$ over all test cases doesn't exceed 1000$$$1000$$$.
output: In each test case, if it is impossible to guarantee fighter 1$$$1$$$ wins, print No$$$\textbf{No}$$$. Otherwise, print Yes$$$\textbf{Yes}$$$ followed by n−1$$$n - 1$$$ lines. Each line should contain two integers a$$$a$$$ and b$$$b$$$ indicating that fighter a$$$a$$$ defeats fighter b$$$b$$$ in a scheduled match. You may print each character in either case, for example YES$$$\textbf{YES}$$$ and yEs$$$\textbf{yEs}$$$ will also be accepted.
